newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold exchange volume at record.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold exchange volume at record.

text.p: Active trading by banks boosted volume to a daily record of 2,490 kilos in the first session on the Istanbul gold exchange on Wednesday, dealers said.
This compared with a previous daily record of 1,930 kilos on August 26, 1996. Volume was 850 kilos on Tuesday morning.
"The bulk of the trade was made by banks buying in dollar terms and selling in lira terms to record profits," a free market dealer said.
Gold finished the first session at $357.10 an ounce and 1,261,800 lira per gram, down from $358.70 and 1,265,500 lira at Tuesday's close, in line with the world trends.
Dealers said physical gold demand from the free market was not significant, although lower prices buoyed purchases.
"Because of the fall in the ounce price, there was a certain amount of physical demand, but most of the demand came from the banks," one bank trader said.
The Turkish currency weakened and stood at 110,000 lira to the dollar at midday, versus 109,460 at Tuesday's close.
Of total gold turnover, 1,385 kilos was in lira terms and the rest in dollars.
